prompt: A production assistant misses its retrieval target for recently amended policies. Replay confirms that the affected amendments are absent from the index; indexing them restores the target on those cases. The vector store and model otherwise meet agreed service levels. What should the feedback loop recommend?

options.text: Replace the architecture: any retrieval miss disproves its design.
Repair freshness triggers with an owner and slice recheck.
Use a larger model; leave index freshness unchanged.
Close the item because overall quality meets its target.

feedback.reason: The failure is localized to freshness while the broader architecture meets targets; a focused iteration and measurable recheck fit the evidence.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A feedback loop should connect the signal to an owner, response, and follow-up measure.
details.scenarioApplication: The failure is localized to freshness while the broader architecture meets targets; a focused iteration and measurable recheck fit the evidence.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Re-architecture becomes appropriate if the required freshness cannot be met with a bounded improvement or the underlying constraint is structural.
details.errorCorrection: Choose a response that addresses the demonstrated failure or changed requirement at its actual boundary.
details.transfer: Use the scope and persistence of the failure to decide whether to iterate or change the architecture.

messages.text: A confirmed freshness defect does not establish that every component or the overall pattern must be replaced.
A stronger model cannot retrieve an amendment absent from the current index.
A passing aggregate does not resolve the affected policy-amendment slice.

prompt: The workflow must return a current authoritative result from an external system within two seconds. Controlled measurements show that the required synchronous call takes 8–12 seconds; the system offers no asynchronous status API, and stale answers are not permitted. Local tuning has not changed this. What should the review conclude?

options.text: Continue prompt tuning to meet the two-second deadline.
Add retries until the slow dependency returns within the deadline.
Escalate the structural limit; revise design or requirement.
Exclude slow in-scope cases and report the remaining latency.

feedback.reason: Repeated evidence shows the bottleneck lies in an external synchronous dependency; more local prompt iteration cannot satisfy the hard deadline.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Feedback should trigger a design decision when measured constraints make the current architecture infeasible.
details.scenarioApplication: Repeated evidence shows the bottleneck lies in an external synchronous dependency; more local prompt iteration cannot satisfy the hard deadline.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A different architecture might require asynchronous work or a revised SLA; it still needs stakeholder approval and an explicit boundary.
details.errorCorrection: Choose a response that addresses the demonstrated failure or changed requirement at its actual boundary.
details.transfer: Use feedback to distinguish tunable weaknesses from structural limits.

messages.text: Prompt tuning cannot make the required external result available before the synchronous dependency returns.
More attempts add work; they do not remove the dependency’s measured minimum response time.
Excluding slow in-scope cases changes the reported population rather than meeting the deadline.

prompt: A release has p95 latency 30% above target for two weeks, but only one region is affected after a network change. The model and retrieval quality metrics remain stable. What is the best next action?

options.text: Rebuild retrieval before investigating the regional route.
Increase token limits and hope response latency improves.
Report the global average and hide the regional breach.
Diagnose the region and verify a targeted route correction.

feedback.reason: The signal is a sustained localized operational regression; the feedback loop should name an owner/action and verify a targeted correction first.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Not every production signal implies a new architecture; isolate the affected component and test a bounded change.
details.scenarioApplication: The signal is a sustained localized operational regression; the feedback loop should name an owner/action and verify a targeted correction first.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If route-level fixes cannot meet the target, bring evidence back for a broader architecture decision.
details.errorCorrection: Choose a response that addresses the demonstrated failure or changed requirement at its actual boundary.
details.transfer: Make the signal actionable, scoped, and tied to a measurable recheck.

messages.text: The regional regression warrants investigation; it does not yet identify retrieval architecture as the cause.
Increasing tokens does not target the suspected regional route and may add latency.
A global average hides the sustained breach experienced by users in the affected region.

prompt: A new safety requirement changes from “flag suspicious output” to “block every unverified external action before execution.” The current design only audits the answer afterward. What should happen?

options.text: Add and test authorization before external actions execute.
Improve the post-action audit dashboard without moving the gate.
Tell the model not to execute unverified actions.
Extend the SLA while retaining the post-action-only control.

feedback.reason: The requirement moved from post-hoc detection to pre-action enforcement, which changes the control boundary; a local telemetry iteration is insufficient.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Feedback and updated stakeholder requirements can invalidate an architecture assumption and justify re-architecture.
details.scenarioApplication: The requirement moved from post-hoc detection to pre-action enforcement, which changes the control boundary; a local telemetry iteration is insufficient.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The revised path still needs a defined owner, policy source, and failure behavior.
details.errorCorrection: Choose a response that addresses the demonstrated failure or changed requirement at its actual boundary.
details.transfer: Compare the new requirement with the actual enforcement point before deciding to iterate.

messages.text: An audit after execution can report the action but cannot block it beforehand.
Prompt instructions do not implement the required trusted pre-action authorization gate.
A longer response target does not move the control ahead of the protected action.

prompt: Quality scores decline for three consecutive weekly reviews. Error rate is flat, so the existing hard-error alert has not fired. The approved governance table requires architect review for a sustained three-week quality trend. What should happen?

options.text: Wait for an error alert; ignore the separate trend trigger.
Invoke trend review with owned diagnosis and follow-up.
Replace the model before diagnosing the quality trend.
Remove the quality metric to preserve the error dashboard.

feedback.reason: The stated quality-trend trigger has been reached independently of the hard-error alert. Review representative evidence, diagnose the source, and assign a measured follow-up.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The stated quality-trend trigger has been reached independently of the hard-error alert. Review representative evidence, diagnose the source, and assign a measured follow-up.
details.scenarioApplication: The stated quality-trend trigger has been reached independently of the hard-error alert. Review representative evidence, diagnose the source, and assign a measured follow-up.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The three-week interval is a scenario rule, not a universal escalation threshold.
details.errorCorrection: Apply the declared trigger and closure criteria to the observed evidence.
details.transfer: Keep signals, decision triggers, owned actions, and measured closure connected.

messages.text: The governance table defines a separate trend trigger; error-rate stability does not cancel it.
The trigger requires diagnosis, not an unsupported conclusion that the model is at fault.
Different metrics can reveal different failures; discarding one hides the trend.

prompt: A one-day p99 latency increase of 40 ms remains inside the agreed budget. The governance table calls for internal monitoring for isolated within-budget changes, with escalation if a sustained trend or breach appears. No such trend or breach is present. What fits this evidence?

options.text: Rewrite the SLA to match the isolated observation.
Declare a critical incident whenever p99 changes.
Record and monitor under the existing trigger rules.
Stop collecting p99 to avoid distracting stakeholders.

feedback.reason: The observation fits the stated internal-monitoring rule. Preserve evidence and watch for the defined escalation conditions rather than treating every movement as a stakeholder decision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The observation fits the stated internal-monitoring rule. Preserve evidence and watch for the defined escalation conditions rather than treating every movement as a stakeholder decision.
details.scenarioApplication: The observation fits the stated internal-monitoring rule. Preserve evidence and watch for the defined escalation conditions rather than treating every movement as a stakeholder decision.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A newly discovered safety or correctness risk can require separate action even while latency remains within budget.
details.errorCorrection: Apply the declared trigger and closure criteria to the observed evidence.
details.transfer: Keep signals, decision triggers, owned actions, and measured closure connected.

messages.text: An isolated within-budget observation does not invalidate the current commitment.
The stated critical or escalation conditions have not occurred.
Removing the metric prevents detection if the change becomes sustained or crosses the budget.

prompt: A targeted indexing fix has passed the affected policy slice and relevant regressions. Freshness monitoring meets the agreed window, an owner has accepted the evidence, and no other open requirement remains. What should the feedback loop do next?

options.text: Close with evidence; retain monitoring and revisit rules.
Keep the item open until every future amendment has been tested.
Replace the architecture despite the passing scoped correction.
Delete the incident record because the fix now passes.

feedback.reason: The declared correction criteria are met. Record the evidence and owner decision, close the scoped item, and retain monitoring and conditions that would reopen it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The declared correction criteria are met. Record the evidence and owner decision, close the scoped item, and retain monitoring and conditions that would reopen it.
details.scenarioApplication: The declared correction criteria are met. Record the evidence and owner decision, close the scoped item, and retain monitoring and conditions that would reopen it.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Closing this item does not establish that all future inputs or every unrelated requirement are validated.
details.errorCorrection: Apply the declared trigger and closure criteria to the observed evidence.
details.transfer: Keep signals, decision triggers, owned actions, and measured closure connected.

messages.text: Future unknown amendments cannot all be tested now; ongoing monitoring handles drift after the evidenced closure.
The successful correction supplies no reason by itself to discard the architecture.
Deleting the record loses the rationale and regression evidence needed for future changes.
